output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday 26 November launch — Inês

HANDOVER PAGE — LAUNCH OF "WHO PAYS AT THE BORDER? CBAM REVENUES AND THE LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES"
Thursday 26 November, European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, room booked by Lindqvist's office.

Inês — this is everything, in the order I would do it. Written on a train on Monday night, so forgive the slightly chaotic shape of it.

WHY I AM NOT THERE
My father is ill, I am with my family, and I am away from Brussels from tonight. I may get back before Thursday and I may not. Please plan on the second version of Thursday, because I do not want you waiting for me.

THE SHORT VERSION
You present. You hold the panel. You carry the corrected number and the argument of the paper. I trust you completely with this — not as a way of making you feel better about my absence, but because it is true. You ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, you know this work better than almost anyone alive, and Thursday's panel is stronger with you on it than with me on it.

And I am sorry. Sorry to hand this over at the last minute, sorry to leave you the number and the press release and the journalists in the same evening, and sorry that the first thing you hear about Thursday is a mess. It is a mess because I made a mistake, not because you did anything wrong.

Below is the detail. Read it once tonight, then work down it in order.

1. THE NUMBER — FIX THIS FIRST, EVERYTHING ELSE DEPENDS ON IT
The headline 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion. Not 2.1 billion. The 2.1 came from an old model run that did not apply the free allocation phase-out.
- PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15 — summary, figure and headline table). Use v7 for anything that goes out or is shown. Do not circulate v6 or anything older.
- Still wrong: the deck (v4, slides 6 and 9) and the press release Hanna sent to 34 Brussels contacts under embargo on Friday, which says 2.1.
- The conclusion of the paper does not change. The headline number does. That is the sentence to use if anyone asks why the release needs reissuing.
- The error is mine. It was mine in the first place and I found it this afternoon. If anyone — journalist, Kessler, anyone — asks who got it wrong, say so plainly: it came from an old run on our side and it was corrected before the launch. Do not absorb blame for it and do not let anyone frame it as your mistake.

2. CORRECTED PRESS RELEASE — BEFORE THE EMBARGO LIFTS
The embargo lifts Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. Thirty-four contacts have the wrong number in their inbox, so this has to happen well before that.
- Ask Hanna to produce a corrected version (v2) of the release and send it to the same list, still under the same embargo, with one line at the top: "Correction: 2030 LDC-relevant CBAM revenue is EUR 1.4 billion (earlier version said EUR 2.1 billion; the underlying error was in an outdated model run)."
- Get that out Tuesday morning, so the two journalists with calls on Wednesday morning already have the right number in hand.
- Check the corrected release end to end: headline, lede, bullet points, any chart caption, any quote from me or Hanna. Search the folder for "2.1" and see what else surfaces.
- Geert knows I am away and can sign off the corrected release if Hanna wants a senior name on it. Ask Hanna to loop him in and copy him, rather than leaving it sitting in a mailbox. If Hanna is stuck on wording, that is exactly what Geert is for.
- Two journalists — one trade newsletter, one Belgian daily — asked for a call before the event. The 14:00 and 15:00 slots on Wednesday are in the calendar, currently "Hanna to confirm". Confirm them with Hanna tomorrow morning and take both. Do not let them wait on an unconfirmed call.
- On those calls, raise the correction yourself before they find it. If they are comparing the number against something else in circulation, hearing it from you first is much better than hearing it from someone else.

3. DECK v4 — SLIDES 6 AND 9
- Slide 9 is the revenue chart, slide 6 also carries 2.1. You built this deck, you know where the numbers are; this should be quick.
- Check every other slide, the appendix slides and the figure captions for 2.1 while you are in there.
- The speaker notes in the deck are mine. Update the lines that quote the revenue figure and keep the rest — it is still the best version of the argument.
- Abena's remote link is in the calendar invite and she tested it. Please test the remote leg yourself on Wednesday morning if you can get into the room, and sit near the laptop on Thursday. In Lisbon you saved my panel when the projector died and nobody in the room noticed anything had gone wrong; do not let the tech become Thursday's story.

4. WEDNESDAY 12:00 — NAMES TO TOMÁS
Final names of everyone from our side have to be with Tomás by Wednesday 12:00 or security will not let them in.
- Lucy Tran is coming with a colleague — get the colleague's full name from Lucy tomorrow morning and send both to Tomás.
- Confirm Kessler is on the list and who is bringing him. Abena is remote, so no badge, but check that Tomás has the right remote-participant instructions for her.
- Send yourself and anyone else from the institute who is coming.

5. THURSDAY — THE RUNNING ORDER, AS CHANGED
Tomás moved things on Friday because of a vote Lindqvist has to get to. The run of show in the folder is out of date; use this version.
- 12:00 — guests at the security entrance; badges from Tomás; light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30 — Lindqvist's welcome (5 minutes).
- 12:35 — presentation, 15 minutes, not 20. That is you.
- 12:50 — panel: Lindqvist moderating, Abena Owusu-Mensah remote, Florian Kessler, you.
- Lindqvist leaves at 13:30 and wants to take at least two questions herself. That gives you forty minutes with her in the room, then the last ten minutes without her. Put the two things that matter — the corrected figure and the pass-through result — on the table before she goes, and do not leave the punchline for after she has left.
- 13:40 — Q&A. 14:00 — close.
- With me absent the panel is three people and two of them are ours. You do not have to be louder than Kessler, only clearer.

6. KESSLER
He told us on 12 November that he would push the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling, so expect it and do not be surprised by it.
- Pass-through: 80% is the central case, annex B runs 40% and 60%, the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say this openly and in that order. Do not get defensive, and do not pretend the sensitivity runs are a footnote — they are the answer.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk, it is section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report. Conceding this buys us the rest of the discussion.
- If he tries to make the whole thing about the 80% figure, do not let him set the frame. Put central case and sensitivity in the same breath, then move the room back to the paper's actual question: what this means for least developed countries. He is an invited guest, not the author of the agenda.
- He may have seen the old 2.1 figure in the draft he commented on. If he quotes it, correct it immediately and plainly: the corrected figure is 1.4, the earlier number came from an outdated run on our side.
- Abena was strong on the LDC side on the call and will probably back you. Give her room to speak rather than covering for her.

7. SMALL THINGS THAT WOULD HELP ME
- Lucy Tran needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers for the Halvorsen grant report, ideally by 4 December. Take a couple of photos of the room and the panel (with Abena on screen) and count heads at the door. Note the numbers in the launch folder, not just in an email.
- Save the final corrected release, the final deck and the attendance count in the launch folder so they do not disappear into threads.
- Keep the calendar invite for Thursday; that is where Abena's link lives.

8. IF SOMETHING NEEDS A DECISION AND I AM NOT THERE
- Hanna: press release, embargo, journalists.
- Geert: sign-off on the corrected release; he knows I am away.
- Tomás: badges, room, timings.
- Me: call me any time before 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday. After that I might not pick up — I am with my family and the phone may be off. If it is genuinely urgent and I am unreachable, Geert decides on the release and Hanna handles the journalists. Neither of them will think less of you for making the call.

One last thing. In Lisbon at the COP side event you rescued my panel when the projector died, and you did it without letting anyone see you sweat. You are far better live than you think you are. Do not be modest on Thursday.

I am sorry, and thank you.

Marieke

reasons: Facts fail: it says the journalists' calls are on Wednesday morning (they are 14:00 and 15:00 that afternoon), and that Tomás moved the timings on Friday (his email came Monday 23 Nov).
